title: Solana permissions are capability flags rather than a role hierarchy, and the Solana Freezer can liquidate where the Ethereum one cannot
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.2.2.1.1 restates the same four roles for Solana, but the permissions are enumerated capabilities rather than named roles. Admin holds `can_freeze_controller`, `can_unfreeze_controller`, `can_manage_permissions`, `can_suspend_permissions`, `can_manage_reserves_and_integrations` and `can_invoke_external_transfer`. Relayer holds `can_execute_swap` and `can_reallocate`, and "may be granted to an address by any address with `can_manage_permissions` privileges and can be revoked by one with `can_suspend_permissions` privileges." Freezer holds `can_freeze_controller`, `can_suspend_permissions` **and `can_liquidate`**.

Splitting grant from suspend across two distinct capabilities reproduces the Ethereum asymmetry — the emergency role can subtract privileges but not add them — while making the rule explicit in data rather than implicit in a role check. The capability model also allows finer combinations than Ethereum's four-role scheme, at the cost of a permission surface a reader must reconstruct flag by flag.

The substantive divergence is `can_liquidate`. On Ethereum the Freezer's power is defined narrowly as removing a compromised relayer; on Solana the same role can also liquidate positions. That is a materially stronger emergency authority handed to a 2-of-5 multisig on the chain where Keel's own relayers are single-signer keys and where governance's reach is weakest.

The reading that makes it coherent: on Ethereum, freezing suffices because Sky Governance can intervene directly and quickly afterwards; on Solana it cannot, so the emergency role must be able to finish the job rather than merely stop the bleeding.
description: Roles carry explicit flags — can_execute_swap, can_reallocate, can_manage_permissions, can_suspend_permissions — and the Solana Freezer holds can_liquidate in addition to freezing and suspending.
